stem: A family asks whether their child's developmental assessment should automatically include many further tests at the first visit. What is the best response?

options.text: Yes, extensive further investigations are always the most important first step
No, further investigations have a limited role, so history, examination, and hearing and vision checks remain central
No assessment is needed unless the school also reports concerns
Yes, because psychometric testing is unnecessary if laboratory tests are ordered
Yes, because developmental delay under 5 years is usually due to a missed blood test

explanation: Further investigations have a limited role. The initial assessment should focus on history, examination, and hearing and vision checks rather than reflexive broad testing.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Assessment: history is critical; examination; always check hearing and vision; limited role for further investigations

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the assessment should not begin with extensive testing as the default approach.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because further investigations have a limited role, and history, examination, and hearing and vision checks remain central to the initial assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because assessment should not be deferred until the school raises concerns.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because psychometric testing remains part of developmental assessment and is not replaced by laboratory tests.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because developmental delay is not usually explained by a single missed blood test.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
